nodes.characterization_summary: Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH precursor shows XRD peaks at 11.8°, 23.6°, 34.3° for NiFe LDH (003), (006), (012) facets and additional peaks for Ni(OH)₂ phases. EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH shows significantly reduced peak intensities indicating poor crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD peaks located at 11.8°, 23.6° and 34.3° correspond to the (003), (006) and (012) facets of NiFe LDH, respectively ... The intensity of the characteristic peaks for the EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH is significantly reduced, indicating the poor crystallinity.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH shows nanosheets vertically and uniformly coated on CFP. EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH maintains uniform nanosheet stacking and overall morphology after electrochemical activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2(c) shows the SEM images of Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH, revealing that the Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH precursor is composed of countless nanosheets ... The SEM images in Fig. 2(f) indicate that the nanosheets still stack uniformly and the overall morphology of nanosheets is well maintained.

properties.description: Low magnification SEM image showing fibrous morphology with scale bar of 10 μm
High magnification SEM image showing detailed nanofiber structure with scale bar of 1 μm
High-magnification SEM image showing nanofiber network
Low-magnification SEM image showing nanofiber morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals nanopores inside EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH nanosheets not present in Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH precursor, attributed to Fe species dissolution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: comparing the TEM results of the Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH and the EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH shown in Fig. 2(d and g), it can be clearly revealed that a huge number of nanopores appear inside the EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH shows lattice spacings of 0.48 nm and 0.27 nm for Ni(OH)₂ (001) and NiFe LDH (012) planes. EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH shows single lattice fringe of 0.49 nm corresponding to Ni(OH)₂ (001) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: two types of lattice stripes are depicted in the Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH, with planar spacings of 0.48 and 0.27 nm ... After electrochemical phase switching, there is only one single lattice fringe in EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH and the lattice spacing is 0.49 nm, which corresponds to the (001) crystal plane of Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, F, C, and O elements throughout EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping images (Fig. S4) indicate the EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH have a homogenous distribution of the Ni, Fe, F, C and O elements throughout the whole detected area.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR shows bands at 1353 cm⁻¹ and 1641 cm⁻¹ for CO₃²⁻ and structural water, and 3617 cm⁻¹ for free O-H groups in both Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH and EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH, indicating maintained layered hydroxide structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Typical FTIR spectra in Fig. 3(a) ... at 1353 and 1641 cm⁻¹ the bands belong to CO₃²⁻ and scissoring mode of structure water, respectively. The sharp and intensive vibration at 3617 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of free O–H groups.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey shows Ni, Fe, F, O, C elements present in both catalysts. High-resolution Fe 2p at 711.9 eV (2p3/2) and 724.4 eV (2p1/2). Ni 2p3/2 shows positive shift of 0.35 eV after activation with Ni³⁺ peak at 856.6 eV. O 1s at 531.2 eV (metal-OH) and 532.1 eV (CO₃²⁻).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3(c) clearly illustrate the presence of Ni, Fe, F, O and C elements in both Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH and EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH ... the peaks at 711.9 and 724.4 eV correlate to Fe 2p3/2 and Fe 2p1/2 ... Ni 2p3/2 delivers a positive shift of 0.35 eV ... emerging peak located at 856.6 eV that can be well corresponded to Ni³⁺ ... O 1s spectrum ... includes two peaks at 531.2 and 532.1 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH has BET surface area of 37 m²/g (19 times higher than Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH at 2 m²/g) with multilevel pore structure and average pore size of 55 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The BET-specific surface area of the EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH is 37 m² g⁻¹ ... which is nearly 19 times as high as that of Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH (2 m² g⁻¹) ... multilevel pore structures with an average pore size of 55 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: EQCM shows EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH absorbs 1.67 times more water than Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance (EQCM) analysis (Fig. 3i) further demonstrates the water absorbed on the EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH is about 1.67 times as much as Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH.

nodes.characterization_summary: EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH exhibits favorable hydrophilicity, fully immersing in water in about 0.1 s, slightly improved from precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the EA-Ni0.82Fe0.18-OH exhibits a relatively favorable hydrophily towards the electrolyte, where can be fully immersed in about 0.1 s.
